taxonomy.note: Current Kew accepts P. foetida and several varieties; Texas is included in the native range.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Bexar is supported at the northern edge of the native South Texas range. Current NPSOT distribution emphasizes Southern Texas Plains and Gulf Coast rather than the Edwards Plateau. Three project target-zone counties were not locked.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Only one exact target-zone county locked confidently in this pass.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not use misidentified San Antonio records of introduced P. lanuginosa/ciliata-type plants as P. foetida evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with texture and smell. Fetid passionflower has densely hairy velvety leaves, a strong unpleasant odor when rubbed, pale flowers with a purple-blue corona, and a finely divided sticky-bracted cage surrounding the flower and fruit.
diagnostic_traits: strong fetid odor when foliage is rubbed
finely divided glandular involucral bracts form a cage
white to pale petals/sepals with purple-blue corona
fruit remains green to yellow-green at maturity in the native Texas concept
